comments.author: Prathamesh Yeole
comments.comment: One trick that helps: add “known equivalent” outputs to the eval set before tuning the agent. For query generation, SQL/KQL/search APIs often have multiple valid forms, so exact-match evals punish harmless variation. I’ve had better signal from checking executable behavior plus a small set of invariants, then saving every false failure as a regression case.

comments.author: Ram Singh Verma
comments.comment: The command that changed Git for me was `git bisect`. In ML codebases, where a "small" data or config change can quietly break behavior, bisect turns a vague regression hunt into a binary search over commits. Which Git command do you think developers learn too late?
